title: Heave of density surfaces caused 54-106% of the 2004-2025 rise of the 0-2000 dbar salinity contrast in the RG Argo grid, while the sea-surface salinity pattern amplified 1.3% per decade
abstract: Question: in the Argo period, is the rise of the 0-2000 dbar ocean salinity contrast (SC2000, a water-cycle indicator) a change of water masses, or is it heave, the vertical motion of density surfaces? Approach: we used the Roemmich-Gilson (RG) Argo grid for January 2004 to September 2026. We calculated the contrast between high- and low-salinity regions on pressure levels and split each annual change into a part along density surfaces (sigma0 and sigma1) and a heave part. We checked the result with about 5,000 raw float profiles per year (2014-2025) and compared adjusted and real-time salinity. Results: in 2004-2025 the contrast rose by 0.66% per decade (95% interval 0.48-0.83) with level-median classes and by 0.47% per decade (0.30-0.64) with one global median. Heave gave 0.37-0.53% per decade in all 12 variants, which is 54-106% of the total. The part along density surfaces was -0.03 to 0.37% per decade. In the raw floats, heave was 0.29% per decade (-0.01 to 0.57) and the part along density surfaces was -0.07% per decade (-0.54 to 0.39). RG gave a faster contrast rise than the floats at the same places (difference -0.39% per decade, -0.84 to -0.03). Real-time salinity drift did not change the contrast trend (-0.08% per decade without one bad 2018 profile). At the sea surface, where heave does not apply, the ENSO-adjusted pattern amplification was 1.31% per decade (0.65-1.96), or 5.9% per K of the 60S-60N SST trend. The 200-2000 dbar trend of 2004-2014 forecast 2015-2025 well; the 0-200 dbar trend did not, because ENSO controls that layer. Limitations: one gridded product; RG has known 2016 and 2019 steps; the heave split uses annual means and sigma0/sigma1, which are noisy in the weakly stratified deep North Atlantic and North Pacific; the profile check uses one day per month; we used no climate models and give no water-cycle estimate.

citations.reason: Real-time Argo salty drift and the RG base-to-near-real-time step; same shared Argo geo files. We show that the drift does not change the salinity contrast.
Shared RG Argo salinity files and access route.
Reports a 0.1 C RG warm step in 2016 that can affect our heave estimate; listed as a limitation.
Cheng et al. 2020: SC2000 index and water-cycle amplification estimate. We show that most of the Argo-era SC2000-type rise is heave.
Durack et al. 2012: surface salinity pattern amplification of about 8% per K; our Argo-era surface rate is 5.9% per K.
Roemmich and Gilson 2009: RG Argo climatology.
